text:
Keep the room calm and keep them still:
They're already overstimulated, so keep crowds and arguments away.
Stop any pacing or exercise to "burn it off": muscle work makes more heat and raises the risk of rhabdomyolysis, where damaged muscle leaks into the blood and can hurt the kidneys.
If they feel a strong urge to keep moving (akathisia), stay with them and help them keep still anyway.
Give fluids only if they're fully alert and not vomiting, and then only small sips of an electrolyte drink. Don't force fluids, food, pills or charcoal on them if they're confused, vomiting or sleepy. The same goes if they're at risk of a seizure, since they could choke.
section: Do this immediately when serotonin toxicity is reasonably suspected:
reader: the friend of someone who may have serotonin syndrome (MDMA on top of an antidepressant, say: shaking, sweating, muscles jerking, burning up), who has just read the signs and must act now, while calling for help and waiting for it

marked.s: I wouldn't wait to see whether it does before doing the other steps.
Put a fan on them and cool damp cloths, and if they're hot, ice packs wrapped in cloth at the neck, armpits or groin.
Fever reducers do not help with heat generated by muscles working this hard.
No crowds or arguments around them.
No pacing or exercise to "burn it off," since muscle work makes more heat and raises the risk of rhabdomyolysis (damaged muscle leaking into the blood, which can hurt the kidneys).
Don't force fluids, food, pills or charcoal on someone who's confused, vomiting, sleepy or at risk of a seizure, since they could choke on them.
exactly what they took, how much and when, including their last dose and any dose they recently increased
While you wait, don't give them niacin: it's this guide's trip killer, but it's unsafe with serotonin syndrome.
DMSO isn't one of these steps either.
Once they're fully alert, I'd consider magnesium chloride by mouth, as in the MDMA section above, especially for MDMA-related jaw tension or muscle twitching.
